_meta.contract: Per-path, NEVER directional. Every after-value below was PRODUCED BY THE REAL ENGINE — the derivation sweep re-runs calculateCashflow and calculateDebtMetrics on live production inputs with the canonical per-loan cost substituted, then diffs every numeric leaf. No value here was hand-derived. Any move OUTSIDE these paths is undeclared and STOPS the tranche (G7). _meta.declarationMethod: DERIVATION SWEEP, not a hand-written list. Three successive captures missed five paths between them because the paths were enumerated by name; the list was deleted (#1561) and replaced by the sweep, so the declaration is complete by construction. All five previously-missed paths appear below without having been named, plus quickMetrics.monthlyLoanRepayments.

feedContract.rule: The migration MUST feed calculateCashflow and calculateDebtMetrics the UNROUNDED canonical monthly cost per loan, at repaymentFrequency MONTHLY, for EVERY loan — no minRepayment filter.
feedContract.why: This is what the sweep measured (t2-loan-cost/route.ts:256-277). It is not a style preference: the per-loan costs ROUNDED to cents sum to 12,779.28, a full cent below the 12,779.29 the engine produced from unrounded inputs. Rounding per loan before summing shifts monthlyLoanRepayments by a cent and cascades into annualLoanRepayments (x12), annualCashflow, savingsRate and debtServiceRatio. On an exact-match contract that is a G7 failure.
feedContract.alsoRequired: The old input filtered out loans with no minRepayment (masterFinancialService.ts:1861) — which is exactly why both interest-only loans read $0 today. The canonical input carries every loan; the filter must be gone, not merely bypassed.

roundingConvention.engineRule: cashflowOrchestrator.ts:259-266 — every ANNUAL leaf is round(UNROUNDED monthly x 12). Annual leaves are NOT derived from annual components.
roundingConvention.t1NoteCorrected: The T1 contract records 'Derive from annual components, never rounded-monthly x12' (.audit/expected-moves-t1.json declaredCorrections, authority VR-045 §2.1). The second half is right and was the real T1 lesson. The first half is NOT the engine's rule — it merely coincided at T1 (both give 180,572.50). At T2 they diverge by a cent: annual components give 133,020.79, the engine emits 133,020.78. This contract takes the MEASURED .78. Declaring .79 from the T1 phrasing would have failed G7 against the engine's own output.

declarationAmendment.amendedBy: Code, in the migration PR — as its FIRST commit, before a line of migration was written (G3 ordering preserved and visible in the git history).
declarationAmendment.what: Two paths added to expectedMoves — `debt.summary.totalRepayments` and `debt.summary.byType.*.repayments` — plus the `structuralAdditions` block below.
declarationAmendment.whyTheSweepMissedThem: The sweep diffs three blocks: `cashflow.*`, `debt.metrics.*` and the quickMetrics mirrors (t2-loan-cost/route.ts — `diffNumericLeaves(snapshot.debt?.metrics, newDebtMetrics, 'debt.metrics')`). `snapshot.debt` has TWO children: `summary` (from `aggregateLoanRepayments`) and `metrics` (from `calculateDebtMetrics`). Only `metrics` was swept. This is the same class of miss the hand-written list made — an unswept sibling of a swept block — and it is the reason the sweep itself is now widened (see `relayWidened`).
declarationAmendment.howItWasFound: Reading the assembly before writing the migration, not from a capture. `masterFinancialService.ts:2039` assigns `quickMetrics.monthlyLoanRepayments = debtSummary.totalRepayments` — the SAME expression. That leaf IS declared (8,816.65 -> 12,779.29), so `debt.summary.totalRepayments` moves by construction and was undeclared. Shipping it would have produced a MOVED-UNDECLARED at G7 that could not be told apart from a mistake.
declarationAmendment.healthScoreChecked: `buildHealthScore` (masterFinancialService.ts:1321) is fed `debtSummary.totalRepayments`, so it was checked rather than assumed. Its savings-rate component is `min(max(savingsRate x 5, 0), 100)`: 59.37 x 5 = 296.85 BEFORE and 43.73 x 5 = 218.65 AFTER — both clamp to 100. debtToIncome reads `totalPrincipal` (unmoved), emergencyFund reads the ACTUALS outflow (unmoved), netWorth unmoved. `healthScore` therefore stays 53 and its mustNotMove entry stands. Computed, not asserted (§19.2).
declarationAmendment.relayWidened: The T2 relay's sweep now diffs `snapshot.debt` WHOLE (both children) instead of `snapshot.debt.metrics` alone, so the next capture measures what this amendment had to derive. The Ratchet applied to the declaration instrument (§23.2.2).

structuralAdditions.why: Leaves ADDED by this tranche. Not moves — nothing that existed changed value — but they change the shape of a captured tree, so they are declared rather than discovered at G7.

items.value: the date of the LATEST linked repayment the resolution consumed; null when the cost did not come from actuals
items.why: VR-046 F1c, added to T2 scope on Reza's instruction 2026-08-03 (T2 INPUT-FEED census, final section). `resolveLoanMonthlyCost` is actuals-first with NO recency requirement, so a repayment from an earlier rate epoch silently becomes today's canonical cost — the Broadbeach case (loan cost $1,191/mo on old-epoch actuals vs tax position $1,271/mo on the stored rate). Recording the age while the producers collapse is cheap; retrofitting means re-opening the producer.
items.scopeRead: The census asks for the basis AND the age. Only the AGE is added here, deliberately: the COST basis is already fully expressible from the existing `usedActuals` / `flooredToInterest` pair, and the RATE basis already has one producer (`effectiveLoanRate.basis`). Copying either into `ResolvedLoanCost` would create a second producer of a fact that already has one (§12.2.1). If Reza meant a wider record, this is the line to redirect.
items.consumers: NONE today — it is the input MON-142's staleness alert needs once MON-145 gives the stored rate a date. It moves no rendered number.

deferrals: D18/X3 — savingsRate below is a STRAIGHT SUBSTITUTION: the whole loan payment is treated as spending. X3 separates PRINCIPAL out of spending and into saving, which changes the numerator's SHAPE, not just its size. Declared here so the after-value is not later mistaken for the X3 answer.

MON-142 — effectiveRate is carried in the capture as evidence only (RATE_STALE on both interest-only loans, implied 6.2697% vs stored 6.690%). No consumer applies it; wiring it is a separate decision awaiting Reza.
